statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-56864 (GO-2026-6180): Client.Lookup in golang.org/x/mod/sumdb trusted unrelated, unauthenticated hashes returned by a checksum database. It is fixed in golang.org/x/mod v0.40.0 and in the go command of Go 1.25.13 and 1.26.6 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6180, https://go.dev/issue/80745, https://go.dev/cl/815000, https://go.dev/cl/815020, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI). Read every published alertmanager-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 36 builds from 0.31.1-r0 to 0.35.0-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64. The only regular files in each package are usr/bin/alertmanager and usr/bin/amtool, two Go programs, and their embedded Go build information gives the Go and module versions below. golang.org/x/mod (v0.32.0 to v0.42.0) appears only in amtool, and the only golang.org/x/mod package compiled into it is golang.org/x/mod/semver; no build contains any function from golang.org/x/mod/sumdb, and neither program is the go command. This was checked against the function names the Go linker records in each binary. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-56864 (GO-2026-6180): a malicious GOSUMDB could serve module content not contained in the transparency log, so a coordinating GOPROXY and GOSUMDB could serve a client malicious module content that evaluating the log would not detect; the fix makes Lookup cache only the authenticated record text. The Go vulnerability database lists the go command (cmd/go) in Go toolchains before 1.25.13 and Go 1.26 before 1.26.6, and Client.Lookup in golang.org/x/mod/sumdb before v0.40.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6180, https://go.dev/issue/80745, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI. The x/mod fix is CL 815000: https://go.dev/cl/815000. For Go 1.26 it was applied to the copy of golang.org/x/mod vendored into the go command by CL 814801 on release-branch.go1.26, "cmd/vendor: fix CVE-2026-56864 in x/mod", which changes src/cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/client.go and is in go1.26.6 and not in go1.26.5: https://go.dev/cl/814801. This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. We read every published golang-1.26-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 15 versions, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1, each matching its repository index checksum. In every build the go command (/usr/lib/go/bin/go) reports the Go release in the package version, and a Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds (*Client).Lookup from the vendored golang.org/x/mod in it, so the vulnerable code is linked into the go command. Every build from 1.26.6-r0 on reports go1.26.6 or later and ships the fixed client.go (Lookup returns cached{text, nil}, the line that change introduces) under /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod; every earlier build (1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.5-r0) reports a Go release before 1.26.6 and ships the unfixed file. The range ends at 1.26.6-r0. The vendored module list names golang.org/x/mod v0.30.1-0.20251115032019-269c237cf350 in every build up to and including the go1.26.6 builds (where the fix is applied directly to the vendored files), then v0.30.1-0.20260813213631-9239cba97fbe and, in the newest builds, v0.40.0. The other golang.org/x/mod versions reported against this package (v0.14.0, v0.19.0, v0.20.0, v0.29.0) are checksum lines in go.sum files of the assembly generators under /usr/lib/go/src/crypto (the _asm directories, checked in the current build), not code the go command uses.

CVE-2026-56864 (GO-2026-6180): A malicious GOSUMDB was capable of serving arbitrary module content not contained within the transparency log. This attack allows for a coordinating GOPROXY and GOSUMDB to serve a client malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log. Go 1.27.0-rc.3 and later Go 1.27 releases, Go 1.26.6 and Go 1.25.13 fix the copy of golang.org/x/mod/sumdb vendored into the go command, and golang.org/x/mod v0.40.0 fixes the module (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6180, https://go.dev/issue/80745, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI, https://go.dev/cl/815000, https://go.dev/cl/815020). On release-branch.go1.27, which the Go 1.27 releases are cut from, the fix is commit a3876703796b (https://go.dev/cl/814861), first released in Go 1.27.0-rc.3. This package is the Go 1.27 toolchain, and its version is the Go release it packages. Every published golang-1.27-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (1.27.0-r0 to the current 1.27.4-r1, x86_64 and aarch64) packages Go 1.27.0 or later, as its go command reports, and ships /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/client.go with the fix (Lookup caches only the authenticated record text), so every published build carries the fix. 1.27.0-r0 is the lowest published build and is the fixed version. The go command uses the golang.org/x/mod copy vendored under /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor: the earlier builds record it as v0.36.1-0.20260813213634-8569e2639ca1, a snapshot that already contains this fix, and the builds from 1.27.1-r1 on vendor v0.40.0. The other golang.org/x/mod versions reported against this package (v0.14.0, v0.19.0, v0.20.0, v0.29.0, v0.33.0) are checksum lines in go.sum files of the assembly generators' _asm directories under /usr/lib/go/src/crypto, not compiled code, and no build contains another copy of golang.org/x/mod. In every build the go command links the advisory's vulnerable function, golang.org/x/mod/sumdb Client.Lookup, as its Go function table (pclntab) shows, so the code is present and the status is FIXED rather than not affected. We also checked the golang-1.27-dev-doc, golang-1.27-dev-oci-config and golang-1.27-dev-fips-oci-config (from the DHI security repository) subpackages built from the same source; with the main packages that is 56 packages in all, each matching the repository index checksum, and the subpackages carry no other copy of golang.org/x/mod.

CVE-2026-56864 (GO-2026-6180): a malicious GOSUMDB could serve module content not contained in the transparency log, so a coordinating GOPROXY and GOSUMDB could serve a client malicious module content that evaluating the log would not detect; the fix makes Lookup cache only the authenticated record text. The Go vulnerability database lists the go command (cmd/go) in Go toolchains before 1.25.13 and Go 1.26 before 1.26.6, and Client.Lookup in golang.org/x/mod/sumdb before v0.40.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6180, https://go.dev/issue/80745, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI. The x/mod fix is CL 815000: https://go.dev/cl/815000. For Go 1.26 it was applied to the copy of golang.org/x/mod vendored into the go command by CL 814801 on release-branch.go1.26, "cmd/vendor: fix CVE-2026-56864 in x/mod", which changes src/cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/client.go and is in go1.26.6 and not in go1.26.5: https://go.dev/cl/814801. This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. We read every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64: 28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, each matching its repository index checksum. In every build the go command (/usr/lib/go/bin/go) reports the Go release in the package version, and a Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds (*Client).Lookup from the vendored golang.org/x/mod in it, so the vulnerable code is linked into the go command. Every build from 1.26.6-0 on reports go1.26.6 or later and ships the fixed client.go (Lookup returns cached{text, nil}, the line that change introduces) under /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod; every earlier build (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.5-0) reports a Go release before 1.26.6 and ships the unfixed file. The range ends at 1.26.6-0. The vendored module list names golang.org/x/mod v0.30.1-0.20251115032019-269c237cf350 in every build up to and including the go1.26.6 builds (where the fix is applied directly to the vendored files), then v0.30.1-0.20260813213631-9239cba97fbe and, in the newest builds, v0.40.0. The other golang.org/x/mod versions reported against this package (v0.14.0, v0.19.0, v0.20.0, v0.29.0) are checksum lines in go.sum files of the assembly generators under /usr/lib/go/src/crypto (the _asm directories, checked in the current build), not code the go command uses.

The vendored module list names golang.org/x/mod v0.30.1-0.20251115032019-269c237cf350 in every build up to and including the go1.26.6 builds (where the fix is applied directly to the vendored files), then v0.30.1-0.20260813213631-9239cba97fbe and, in the newest builds, v0.40.0. The other golang.org/x/mod versions reported against this package (v0.14.0, v0.19.0, v0.20.0, v0.29.0) are checksum lines in go.sum files of the assembly generators under /usr/lib/go/src/crypto (the _asm directories, checked in the current build), not code the go command uses.

CVE-2026-56864 (GO-2026-6180): A malicious GOSUMDB was capable of serving arbitrary module content not contained within the transparency log. This attack allows for a coordinating GOPROXY and GOSUMDB to serve a client malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log. Go 1.27.0-rc.3 and later Go 1.27 releases, Go 1.26.6 and Go 1.25.13 fix the copy of golang.org/x/mod/sumdb vendored into the go command, and golang.org/x/mod v0.40.0 fixes the module (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6180, https://go.dev/issue/80745, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI, https://go.dev/cl/815000, https://go.dev/cl/815020). On release-branch.go1.27, which the Go 1.27 releases are cut from, the fix is commit a3876703796b (https://go.dev/cl/814861), first released in Go 1.27.0-rc.3. This package is the Go 1.27 toolchain, and its version is the Go release it packages. Every published golang-1.27-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.27.0-0 to the current 1.27.4-18, amd64 and arm64) packages Go 1.27.0 or later, as its go command reports, and ships /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/client.go with the fix (Lookup caches only the authenticated record text), so every published build carries the fix. 1.27.0-0 is the lowest published build and is the fixed version. The go command uses the golang.org/x/mod copy vendored under /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor: the earlier builds record it as v0.36.1-0.20260813213634-8569e2639ca1, a snapshot that already contains this fix, and the builds from 1.27.4-1 on vendor v0.40.0. The other golang.org/x/mod versions reported against this package (v0.14.0, v0.19.0, v0.20.0, v0.29.0, v0.33.0) are checksum lines in go.sum files of the assembly generators' _asm directories under /usr/lib/go/src/crypto, not compiled code, and no build contains another copy of golang.org/x/mod. In every build the go command links the advisory's vulnerable function, golang.org/x/mod/sumdb Client.Lookup, as its Go function table (pclntab) shows, so the code is present and the status is FIXED rather than not affected. We also checked the golang-1.27-dev-oci-config, golang-1.27-dev-fips-oci-config (from the DHI security repository) and golang-1.27-dev-dbgsym (debug symbol) packages built from the same source; with the main packages that is 200 packages in all, each matching the repository index checksum, and the subpackages carry no other copy of golang.org/x/mod.
